ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

An early atrial impulse

A 42-year-old reports occasional brief fluttering. ECG shows an early P wave with a different contour from the surrounding sinus P waves, followed by a narrow QRS. The underlying rhythm is otherwise normal. Which diagnosis best explains this isolated event?

  1. Premature atrial contraction
  2. Premature ventricular contraction
  3. Complete atrioventricular block
  4. Sinus arrest
  5. Ventricular escape beat
Answer and explanation

Premature atrial contraction

An early ectopic P wave with conducted ventricular activation identifies a PAC.

Option explanations

Premature atrial contraction: An early ectopic P wave with conducted ventricular activation identifies a PAC.

Premature ventricular contraction: A PVC typically begins with a premature broad QRS without a preceding ectopic P wave.

Complete atrioventricular block: Complete block produces dissociated atrial and ventricular rhythms.

Sinus arrest: Sinus arrest produces a pause rather than an early P wave.

Ventricular escape beat: An escape beat occurs late after a pause, not prematurely.
